# Contents - **Neg** operator for type [real](#real) - **Neg** operator for types [`float16`, `float`, `double`](#float) - **Neg** operator for types [`int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`](#int) Based on ONNX documentation [Neg version 13](https://onnx.ai/onnx/operators/onnx__Neg.html#neg-13). Revision 2026-10-03: first issue of this specification, based on ONNX opset 14, in which **Neg** is at version 13. # **Neg** (real) ## Signature Definition of operator **Neg** signature: $Y = \text{Neg}(X)$ where - $X$: input tensor - $Y$: result of the element-wise negation of $X$ ## Restrictions [General restrictions](./../common/general_restrictions.md) are applicable. No specific restrictions apply to the **Neg** operator. ## Function [E_NEG_REAL_FUNC_0010]
 **Part 1.** Operator **Neg** computes the negation of the input tensor $X$ element-wise and stores the result in tensor $Y$. **Part 2.** For any [tensor index](./../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $Y$: $$ Y[i] = -X[i] $$ where - $X[i]$ is the element of $X$ at index $i$, - $-X[i]$ is the opposite of $X[i]$ in $\mathbb{R}$. The negation is exact: $Y[i]$ is the opposite in $\mathbb{R}$ of $X[i]$, with no approximation, and $X[i] + Y[i] = 0$ for every element. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. Its single element is negated, and $Y$ is a rank-0 tensor. **Zero-sized dimensions.** Tensor $X$ may have a zero-sized dimension. The corresponding dimension of $Y$ then has size $0$, and $Y$ is empty. [END]
 The effect of the operator is illustrated on the following example. ### Example $$ X = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -4.5 & 0 \end{bmatrix} $$ $$ Y = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 4.5 & 0 \end{bmatrix} $$ The negation is exact for every element, and the opposite of $0$ is $0$. ## Error conditions None of the conditions of the list applies to real numbers: the negation is exact and total, so that the result is the one specified by [E_NEG_REAL_FUNC_0010](#E_NEG_REAL_FUNC_0010) for every operand, and no invalid operation, no overflow and no division by zero can occur. No error condition. ## Attributes Operator **Neg** has no attribute. ## Inputs ### $\text{X}$: real tensor The tensor whose elements are negated. #### Constraints No constraint applies to input $X$. ## Outputs ### $\text{Y}$: real tensor Tensor $Y$ is the element-wise negation of $X$. #### Constraints - `[E_NEG_REAL_CONSTR_Y_0010]` Shape definition - Statement: Tensor $Y$ has the shape of $X$. # **Neg** (float) where float is in {`float16`, `float`, `double`}. The three types share one semantics: the IEEE 754 standard defines the same negation for all of them, and they differ only by their precision and by the range of the values they represent. ## Signature Definition of operator **Neg** signature: $Y = \text{Neg}(X)$ where - $X$: input tensor - $Y$: result of the element-wise negation of $X$ ## Restrictions [General restrictions](./../common/general_restrictions.md) are applicable. No specific restrictions apply to the **Neg** operator. ## Function [E_NEG_FLOAT_FUNC_0010]
 **Part 1.** Operator **Neg** computes the negation of the input tensor $X$ element-wise according to IEEE 754 floating-point semantics and stores the result in tensor $Y$. **Part 2.** For any [tensor index](./../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $Y$: $$ Y[i] = -_{(\text{f})} X[i] $$ where $-_{(\text{f})}$ is the negation of the floating-point type of $X$, i.e. $-_{(\text{f16})}$, $-_{(\text{f32})}$ or $-_{(\text{f64})}$ according to that type. The negation of a floating-point number is exact: $Y[i]$ is the value of the type of $X$ whose sign is the opposite of the sign of $X[i]$ and whose magnitude is the magnitude of $X[i]$. No rounding takes place, so that no result is inexact, and the magnitude of the result is a magnitude of the type of $X$, so that no result exceeds the largest finite value of that type. **Values of the operands.** The operand may be any of the values of the type of $X$, including the special numbers $\pm 0$, $\pm\text{inf}$ and NaN. The cases are: - if $X[i]$ is a finite non-zero value, $Y[i]$ is the value of the type of $X$ with the opposite sign and the same magnitude; - if $X[i]$ is $+0$, $Y[i]$ is $-0$, and if $X[i]$ is $-0$, $Y[i]$ is $+0$; - if $X[i]$ is $+\text{inf}$, $Y[i]$ is $-\text{inf}$, and if $X[i]$ is $-\text{inf}$, $Y[i]$ is $+\text{inf}$; - if $X[i]$ is NaN, $Y[i]$ is a NaN. The sign and the payload of a NaN are not specified by IEEE 754, so that every quiet NaN of the type of $X$ is a conforming result. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. Its single element is negated, and $Y$ is a rank-0 tensor. **Zero-sized dimensions.** Tensor $X$ may have a zero-sized dimension. The corresponding dimension of $Y$ then has size $0$, and $Y$ is empty. [END]
 The effect of the operator is illustrated on the following example. ### Example $$ X = \begin{bmatrix} 1.5 & -2.25 & \text{+0} & \text{-0} & \text{+inf} & \text{-inf} & \text{NaN} \end{bmatrix} $$ $$ Y = \begin{bmatrix} -1.5 & 2.25 & \text{-0} & \text{+0} & \text{-inf} & \text{+inf} & \text{NaN} \end{bmatrix} $$ The negation is exact: it reverses the sign of the operand and leaves its magnitude unchanged. The negation of $+0$ is $-0$ and the negation of $-0$ is $+0$; the negation of an infinity is the infinity of the opposite sign; the negation of a NaN is a NaN, whose sign and payload are not specified. ## Error conditions | Condition | Disposition | | -------- | ------- | | Invalid operation, i.e. an operation of IEEE 754 section 7.2 | nominal: specified by [E_NEG_FLOAT_FUNC_0010](#E_NEG_FLOAT_FUNC_0010); the negation introduces no invalid operation, and a NaN operand gives a NaN result | | Overflow, i.e. a result whose magnitude exceeds the largest finite value of the type | nominal: specified by [E_NEG_FLOAT_FUNC_0010](#E_NEG_FLOAT_FUNC_0010); the result has the magnitude of the operand, so that no result exceeds the largest finite value of the type | | Division by zero | not applicable: the operator performs no division, so that the condition cannot occur | Every condition that applies to the floating-point types is part of the nominal behavior of the operator; none of them is an error. No error condition. ## Attributes Operator **Neg** has no attribute. ## Inputs ### $\text{X}$: floating-point tensor The tensor whose elements are negated. #### Constraints - `[E_NEG_FLOAT_CONSTR_X_0010]` Type consistency - Statement: Tensors $X$ and $Y$ have the same type. ## Outputs ### $\text{Y}$: floating-point tensor Tensor $Y$ is the element-wise negation of $X$. #### Constraints - `[E_NEG_FLOAT_CONSTR_Y_0010]` Shape definition - Statement: Tensor $Y$ has the shape of $X$. - `[E_NEG_FLOAT_CONSTR_Y_0020]` Type consistency - Statement: see constraint [E_NEG_FLOAT_CONSTR_X_0010](#E_NEG_FLOAT_CONSTR_X_0010) on tensor $X$. # **Neg** (int) where int is in {`int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`}. The four types share one semantics: each of them is an $n$-bit signed type, whose values range from $-2^{n-1}$ to $2^{n-1}-1$, and the negation of a value of that type is the value of the type that represents its opposite modulo $2^n$. ## Signature Definition of operator **Neg** signature: $Y = \text{Neg}(X)$ where - $X$: input tensor - $Y$: result of the element-wise negation of $X$ ## Restrictions [General restrictions](./../common/general_restrictions.md) are applicable.
